At 8:36 AM ET this morning, Meta (NASDAQ:META) published "Meta launches enterprise platform, MongoDB CEO exits" to its newsroom, confirming it hired MongoDB (NASDAQ:MDB) CEO CJ Desai as chief enterprise platform officer. Enterprise software repriced within minutes. Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) fell 4.23% to $224.13, ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW) fell 4.99% to $128.85 and Snowflake (NYSE:SNOW) fell 4.06% to $322.30. MongoDB dropped 20.9% to $324.54.

clasesdeperiodismo / BY-SA 2.0

The buyer got punished too. Meta slipped 3.97% to $721.83, four days after a 52-week high of $777.59 on Sept. 24, 2026.

What the Event Actually Covers

Two things are confirmed: the platform launch and the Desai hire. Everything else is intent. Available disclosures attach no pricing, customer list or revenue target to the platform, so none is assumed here.

The best map of scope is Meta's July 29, 2026 earnings call. Mark Zuckerberg, CEO at the time of that call, said "we see a large enterprise opportunity to sell to businesses, including APIs, business agents, and many more." He described pricing as "a mix of subscriptions, volume-based pricing" plus results-based fees. Meta business agents already serve more than 1 million businesses weekly on WhatsApp and Messenger.

Who Gets Hurt, Sized Against Their Businesses

Meta carries a $1.59 trillion market cap and booked $59.36B in Q2 advertising revenue. Enterprise revenue is undisclosed and, for now, a rounding error beside the ad engine. The spending is concrete: 2026 capex guidance of $130-145B.

title: Binance to Support SpaceX and QQQ Token Airdrops — Here’s Who Qualifies
detail:
Binance to Support SpaceX and QQQ Token Airdrops — Here’s Who Qualifies
Giuseppe Ciccomascolo
Mon, September 28, 2026 at 8:22 AM MDT 4 min read
MARSCOIN-USD
SPCX
QQQ
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Binance will distribute SPCXB and QQQB to eligible MARSCOIN and 牛来 holders. Learn the 10,000-token threshold, snapshot rules and payout timing. | Credit: CCN.com

Key Takeaways

Binance will distribute SPCXB to eligible MARSCOIN holders and QQQB to eligible 牛来 holders, with the first payout planned for early October.

The exchange will take one random snapshot daily. A balance counts only on days when it exceeds 10,000 tokens.

Rewards will combine project-allocated tokens with additional tokens funded by 30% of Binance's spot trading fees for MARSCOIN and 牛来.

Binance will distribute tokenized SpaceX and Invesco QQQ Trust assets to eligible holders of two other tokens, bringing their existing rewards programs onto the exchange.

Under its Sept. 28 announcement, MarsCoin (MARSCOIN) holders can receive SpaceX-linked SPCXB, while holders of 牛来, also called Niu Lai, can receive QQQB.

Binance plans to start counting eligible holdings from September and make the first distribution in early October. The exchange will combine tokens allocated by the two projects with additional rewards funded from trading fees on Binance.

Holding either token does not, by itself, guarantee a payout: daily balance thresholds, account status and regional restrictions all apply.

Who Qualifies for the SPCXB and QQQB Airdrops?

Binance will take one random snapshot each day during each calendar month. A MARSCOIN or 牛来 balance counts for that day only if it exceeds 10,000 tokens.

Binance will add a user's valid daily holdings across the month, then calculate their share of rewards against the total valid holdings of other eligible users. It will calculate the two tokens separately.

The snapshots cover Spot, Funding, Margin and Simple Earn Flexible accounts. Binance will exclude tokens pending deposit or withdrawal, undistributed interest, and holdings in Binance Alpha.

It will also exclude MARSCOIN or 牛来 liabilities from Margin or Crypto Loans; users with net liabilities may have to return an equivalent amount of any airdropped SPCXB or QQQB.

Users must complete identity verification and live in an eligible jurisdiction. Binance says access to its bStocks products also affects reward eligibility.

Those conditions matter because SPCXB and QQQB are tokenized securities, and product availability differs by region. The exchange says trading, deposits, withdrawals and Earn services will continue during the airdrop.

Where Do the Rewards Come From?

The airdrop has two components. First, Binance will pass along SPCXB and QQQB that the respective projects allocate onchain to qualifying MARSCOIN and 牛来 holders.

Second, Binance will use 30% of the spot trading fees it collects on MARSCOIN and 牛来 to fund additional platform rewards, paid in SPCXB and QQQB, respectively.

Should You Buy QQQ or VUG Right Now? Here's What History Suggests.
David Dierking, The Motley Fool

QQQ
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The Invesco QQQ ETF (NASDAQ: QQQ) is one of the market's best-performing exchange-traded funds (ETFs) of the past 15 years, earning an annual average of 20% over that time frame. That would seemingly make it an easily defensible choice to add to your portfolio.

The Vanguard Growth ETF (NYSEMKT: VUG), however, has put up a pretty strong track record of its own. Its 15-year average annual return has been a modestly lower 17.5%, but I'd argue that it might be better positioned for future growth.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

For me, the choice between two seemingly similar ETFs comes down to the investment strategy. How are the portfolios being built, and is that construction smart? Can these portfolios deliver on their objective, and will they do it in a way that's sensible and logical?

With these two funds, the decision has less to do with historical performance and more to do with whether you're getting what you think you're getting.

Source: Getty Images.
QQQ: Great track record with a curious strategy

The Invesco QQQ ETF tracks the Nasdaq-100 index. Its strategy is very simple: invest in the 100 largest non-financial stocks traded on the Nasdaq (NASDAQ: NDAQ) exchange.

Many people don't mind that strategy because of its performance. A lot of the major tech companies have chosen to list on the Nasdaq, so the Nasdaq-100 index becomes very top-heavy and saturated with tech stocks. It gives this fund the impression that it's a tech ETF, but that's more by pure coincidence than anything.

While Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), and Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG)(NASDAQ: GOOGL) are the fund's biggest holdings, it's some of the stocks further down the list that show what a mixed bag this index really is.

Also in the portfolio are Walmart (NASDAQ: WMT), Costco Wholesale (NASDAQ: COST), Amgen (NASDAQ: AMGN), Linde (NASDAQ: LIN), T-Mobile (NASDAQ: TMUS), and PepsiCo (NASDAQ: PEP). That's two big-box retailers, a biotech, a chemical company, a telecom, and a consumer goods manufacturer.

You don't see that in too many "tech" ETFs.
